Nebraska Campaign Finance

Contributions, loans and spending reported to the Nebraska Accountability and Disclosure Commission, 2022–2026, collected from the FirstTuesday bulk extracts. Cross-source search across contracts, contributions and lobbying is in the Public Records Hub.

25,173 contributors · 926 filers, 2022–2026. Only itemized transactions are searchable here — contributions at or below the roughly $250 aggregate threshold are reported as lump sums on a committee's summary page, not as line items, so a small donor's total here is often an undercount, never an overcount.

Read this before quoting it

Summing the amount column over-counts. The state fans one transaction out over several rows that share an ID — an independent expenditure against five candidates is five rows, a contribution to a slate committee is one row per candidate — repeating the amount on each. Every row carries an include_in_total flag; this page's totals sum only where it is true. For 2022 contributions alone that is the difference between $68,865,363 and $68,955,221.
  • Only itemized transactions appear. Contributions below the roughly $250 aggregate threshold are reported as lump sums on a committee's summary page, never as line items. Totals built from line items undercount small money.
  • Amendments overwrite; there is no history. The amended column is a bare Y/N flag. A corrected filing replaces the original in place, so two pulls on different dates can disagree with no audit trail. Every dated pull is archived here because the state keeps no such record.
  • Each extract is a snapshot, not a ledger. Late and corrected transactions appear retroactively in prior years. No year is ever final.
  • A loan is not a contribution, and a bare pledge is not money — both are kept out of the contributions table on purpose. A $50,000 self-loan is borrowed, not raised.
  • 2022–2026 only. This is the FirstTuesday era. Filings from 1985–2021 sit in a separate, frozen state dataset that is not collected here yet.
  • Federal candidates file with the FEC, not the NADC.
  • Home addresses are never shown here. The state's raw extract carries a street address for individual contributors; this page shows city and state only. The state's own site has the rest, for anyone who wants to look a filer up there directly.

Provenance

Downloaded from the NADC's bulk data page, most recently 2026-09-08. The state publishes column layouts, but the expenditures layout misnames three of its own columns and the transaction-type lists in both PDFs do not match the data, so the scraper checks every header against a confirmed layout and fails loudly rather than guessing.

Built 2026-09-15. Method, caveats and open work are in the project README. No analytics, no tracking, nothing loads from a third party.
